subject: Ephemeral signing proxy + escrow authorization for Greenfield Health private deploy
messages:
From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@greenfield.health>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenfield.health
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Keystore approach for private VPC deploy — quick sync request

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options last week. We’re kicking off the security review and need to confirm the proposed model for signing/encryption inside our VPC. A few items we need clarity on:

- Where customer root keys live (customer HSM vs Redwood-managed escrow).
- How Redwood’s proxy can perform short-lived signing without gaining persistent access to customer key material.
- Emergency access / unseal flow and audit evidence for SOC2/HIPAA.
- Network ports/subnets required for the proxy and any egress constraints.

I attached the current diagram and our SOC2 questionnaire. Can someone from the tech/security team confirm whether the ephemeral-signer-proxy pattern you mentioned is acceptable and what controls you need to implement it?

Regards,
Sara
Sara Chen
Security Architect, Greenfield Health
security@greenfield.health

Attachments: arch-diagram-v3.pdf, greenfield-soc2-questions.xlsx
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Chen <sara.chen@greenfield.health>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Keystore approach for private VPC deploy — quick sync request

Folks — forwarding Greenfield’s questions. They’re evaluating a VPC/on-prem style deployment and want to adopt a model where the customer keeps custody of the long-term root in their HSM but allows an on-VPC proxy that performs ephemeral signing for Redwood requests.

High level ask: confirm the threat model and list the minimum controls (network, audit, operator separation) we’d need to propose so they pass SOC2/HIPAA checks. I sketched a few options below; happy to discuss on a quick call.

My initial thoughts (for discussion):
- Customer-owned root key stays inside customer HSM (BYOK import or local generation). Redwood never stores private material.
- A small, customer-controlled signing service inside their VPC gets custody of short-lived derived keys (wrapped/unwrapped by HSM APIs). Redwood routes signing requests to that proxy over a tightly scoped mTLS channel with per-request ephemeral tokens.
- Ephemeral key material should be 15–60 min TTL; requests must include nonce and replay protection.
- Audit: the signing proxy must log per-request attestation (signature counter, HSM key-slot id, request id) and forward signed audit bundles to the customer’s SIEM.

Questions for the group: what network ports/subnet placement do we require and what emergency access (dual-sig, break-glass) flows do we support?

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Chen <sara.chen@greenfield.health>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Keystore approach for private VPC deploy — quick sync request

Thanks for flagging — I reviewed Greenfield’s diagram. A few concrete notes and constraints from the on-prem ops side:

1) Key custody model
- Prefer customer-generated root keys (local HSM generation) with a one-time import record if they must import. Import requires documented transporter custody and PKCS#11/PKCS12 artifact with strict shipping — we should avoid imports unless mandated.

2) Ephemeral signing proxy design
- The proxy should be a small service inside the customer subnet that runs as a short-lived container VM and talks to the HSM over the vendor’s API (PKCS#11 or KMIP).
- We recommend the proxy not hold unwrapped key bytes in memory longer than the signing op. Use HSM-native signing where possible (server-side op).
- For performance-critical paths, the proxy can request an HSM-wrapped ephemeral key (derived via HSM KDF) where the wrapped blob is stored in an in-memory keystore guarded by an operator-less agent and automatically zeroized on TTL expiry.

3) Authorization and tokens
- Redwood issues per-session signed tokens (JWT with short expiry) bound to a client cert and request nonce. Tokens must be single-use and recorded in both Redwood and customer logs.

4) Emergency unseal / break-glass
- We can offer a dual-signer emergency flow: two customer operators sign an unseal authorization inside the HSM’s operator quorum; a transient operator access token is minted and attested by HSM logs.
- All emergency actions generate an auditable bundle (operator ids, timestamps, base64 HSM audit snippet) that is pushed to the customer’s archive before a key operation is allowed.

5) Network & egress
- The proxy needs outbound connectivity only to Redwood’s control-plane endpoint for token validation (mTLS on port 443). No inbound openings from Redwood into customer subnets.
- Optional: dedicated NAT for proxy egress so customer can control and monitor external traffic.

I’ll draft a short secure-deploy checklist we can share with Greenfield. Any additions from Kim or Jonas?

-Marissa
Senior Applied Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Chen <sara.chen@greenfield.health>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Keystore approach for private VPC deploy — quick sync request

Couple of practical additions from the HSM/ops playbook perspective:

- Evidence and telemetry: we need to provide Greenfield with sample HSM audit extracts and a mapping table that ties HSM event IDs to the actions we propose (sign, wrap, unwrap, operator-auth). That will make their SOC2 evidence collection straightforward.

- Rotation and rewrap cadence: recommend a two-tier cadence:
  * Ephemeral keys: TTL = 15–60 min, rotate automatically; no long-term storage.
  * Root keys: annual review and rewrap with customer sign-off; rewrap performed inside HSM with customer operator quorum.

- Test hooks: we should include a simulated failover drill (offline HSM scenario) where the proxy fails closed and Redwood falls back to a pre-agreed cold-signing process (customer-signed offline token exchange). This drill will be part of acceptance.

- Attachments for Greenfield: anonymized HSM audit snippet, sample proxy deployment manifest, and our recommended snippet for mTLS client cert rotation.

-Kim
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Chen <sara.chen@greenfield.health>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Keystore approach for private VPC deploy — quick sync request

Added a few operational constraints:

- Deployment topology: place proxy in a private subnet with no public IP, behind internal ALB that only allows traffic from the Redwood control-plane CIDR via mTLS. We recommend using a dedicated ENI or VLAN for the proxy cluster to limit blast radius.

- Scaling and batching: implement a local request queue with per-instance token buckets to avoid overwhelming the HSM with concurrent sign ops. Prefer batched HSM operations (where the vendor supports multi-sign) to improve latency/cost.

- Secrets handling: the proxy must not persist HSM unwrapped keys. Any wrapped ephemeral blob must be sealed to local memory only and cleared on container termination. Also, ensure kernel-level seccomp or similar prevents core dumps containing key material.

- Evidence delivery: require the signing proxy to publish signed per-batch evidence objects to a pre-configured S3/GCS endpoint within Greenfield’s controlled account. Each evidence object includes batch id, request ids, HSM event id, and aggregated counters.

I’ll author the deploy checklist and run it by Kim for HSM artifact examples. Jasmine, can you schedule a 30-min call with Greenfield tomorrow morning to walk through the checklist?

-Jonas
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Keystore approach for private VPC deploy — quick sync request

Hi Sara — thanks for the detailed ask and for sharing the diagram. Quick summary of what we’ll deliver before the call:

1) Secure-deploy checklist (network ports, certs, NAT, evidence endpoints).
2) HSM audit mapping and an anonymized sample audit bundle.
3) Ephemeral-proxy manifest + runtime constraints (seccomp, memory zeroize, TTL enforcement).
4) Emergency unseal flow doc (dual-op signer, evidence bundling).

We think the proposed ephemeral-signer-proxy pattern is acceptable if Greenfield holds the root key inside their HSM and the proxy meets the controls above. The team will bring the checklist to the call tomorrow at 09:30 PT.

Call invite: https://meet.redwood.ai/ical/greenfield-keystore-sync

Best,
Jasmine
